long_biography.plain_text:
Making Schindler's List prompted Steven Spielberg to turn a film project into a permanent historical institution. He founded the Survivors of the Shoah Visual History Foundation to record Holocaust survivor testimony, building an archive that later moved to the University of Southern California. Its collections now support research, education and public access.

Film preservation provides another institutional expression of Spielberg's work. He helped establish The Film Foundation and remains on its board as it restores threatened motion pictures and teaches the language of cinema. At Amblin Entertainment, his chairmanship keeps him involved in film, television and digital-media projects beyond the features he directs himself.
